title: Sleep Trackers May Make You Feel More Tired
paragraphs: Sleep-tracking devices and apps have become increasingly popular, with millions of people using smartwatches and fitness bands to monitor how long and how well they sleep. In the United States alone, the market for sleep-tracking devices was worth about $5 billion in 2023. However, a new study from Norway suggests that for some people, tracking their sleep may actually cause more harm than good.

The study was carried out by researchers at the University of Bergen and published in the journal Frontiers in Psychology in March 2026. The researchers surveyed 1,002 adults in Norway who used sleep apps, which collect information from sensors in wearable devices. Most of the participants used smartwatches. The participants were asked about the positive and negative effects the apps had on them.

For many people, the apps were helpful. The most common benefit, reported by 48% of participants, was learning more about their sleep. In addition, 15% said that the apps had actually improved their sleep.

However, the apps also had downsides. The most common negative effect was worrying more about sleep, which was reported by 17% of participants. A small number, 2.3%, said their sleep had become worse.

The researchers found that people who already had symptoms of insomnia were more likely to experience these negative effects, including stress and worry. Age also played an important role. Younger adults were more strongly affected by the apps than older adults, both positively and negatively.

Experts have a name for an unhealthy obsession with achieving perfect sleep, which is often linked to sleep trackers. It is called "orthosomnia." The term was first used in 2017 by researchers in the US, who described patients who became anxious when their trackers showed that they were not getting enough sleep. Worrying about sleep can, in turn, make it harder to sleep.
It is also worth remembering that most consumer sleep trackers do not measure sleep in the same way as a medical sleep study, so their results are not always accurate.

The researchers suggest that people who feel stressed by their sleep apps should learn more about what the devices measure and how accurate they are. If that does not help, they recommend taking the device off at night or turning off notifications.
